item.title: Spur Enrichment for Splunk - v1.1.2 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

`ip\=X` searches against non-Spur sourcetypes silently returned zero results after installing the Spur TA. Indexed-field stanzas in `fields.conf` (`ip`, `feed_type`, `infrastructure`, `tunnel_operator`, `anonymous_tunnel_operator`) were declared globally, so Splunk shadowed search-time extractions for those field names in every other sourcetype.

Stanzas are now scoped to `sourcetype::spur_feed::\<field>`. `sourcetype\=spur_feed ip\=X` queries still hit the TSIDX; no reindex, no query rewrites.


Description:
Official Spur Splunk Application. Enhance your Splunk experience with the Spur Enrichment for Splunk App. This application integrates with Spur products, providing you with enriched data and insights right in your Splunk environment. Generate events based on IP inputs, enrich existing events with data from the Spur Context API, and insert feed data into a Splunk index with our modular input feature. The Spur Splunk App requires an active Spur subscription and specific user privileges for installation. Once installed, you can utilize our search commands and modular input features to generate and enrich your data. Get the most out of your data with the Spur Splunk App. Download today and start exploring your data in new ways.

item.title: AI Workbench - v0.9.7 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

Release notes — AI Assistent for Splunk

This file tracks every customer-visible change.

Format: Keep a Changelog. Dates
are ISO-8601. App version in default/app.conf always matches the
top entry.

0.9.7 — 2026-05-26

Authoring, sharing & promotion model — MVP slice. End users can
now author their own private templates via natural language inside the
Ask tab; the LLM composes the template and a server-side REST handler
enforces sharing=private + owner_user=<caller> + schema /
reference validation regardless of what the LLM emits. See
instructions/AUTHORING_AND_PROMOTION_SPEC.md
for the full design + tasks/AUTHORING_HANDOFF.md
for what shipped in this release vs what's deferred.

Added

  • Sharing scope on templates + skills: new sharing enum
    (private / bu / org / global) + owner_user + owner_org_short
  • owner_bu_short fields. Legacy org_short / bu_short kept for
    one release (dual-read; removed in 0.9.8). Pre-0.9.7 rows are
    back-fillable at read time — no migration script required.
  • 2 new system templates seeded:
  • Create user template — describe a use case in plain English;
    the LLM authors a private template you own.
  • Update user template — refine one of your own private
    templates via natural language; diff narrative on return.
  • 2 new system skills seeded (admin-only, included automatically
    by the authoring templates):
  • template-authoring-discipline — composition rules + skill
    inclusion rules + scope/ownership rules + refusal patterns for
    cross-cutting authoring concerns.
  • prompt-injection-defense-on-authored-content — patterns the
    LLM refuses inside untrusted user descriptions during authoring
    (scope-escalation, owner-spoofing, skill-back-door, guardrail-
    bypass, role-elevation, system-impersonation).
  • 2 new write tools exposed to the LLM:
  • splunk_create_user_template — POST to
    /services/itmip_llm/user_templates/user_create.
  • splunk_update_user_template — POST to
    /services/itmip_llm/user_templates/user_update.
    Both go through a server-side validation chain (quota of 25 private
    templates per user, name uniqueness with auto-suffix, field shapes,
    ASCII-only on user-facing fields, skill-reference visibility,
    forbidden-content scan) before persisting.
  • itmip_authoring_changes KVStore audit collection. Every
    authoring action — create, update, override-attempts that the
    server silently corrected — emits a row with
    attempted_override_fields[], errors[], by_user, tenant_*,
    authoring_mode=llm_mediated. Read admin-only; backed up daily
    with the rest of the critical collections.
  • Visibility filter (filterByUserAccess + filterSkillsByUserAccess)
    now switches on sharing first, then falls back to dependent_apps +
    required_roles checks. End users see their own private templates;
    other users do not. Admins inherit the existing "see everything"
    surface via separate code paths (Templates tab).
  • Auto-refresh of templates after authoring. The dispatcher fires
    a ca:templates-changed window event after every successful
    splunk_create_user_template / splunk_update_user_template tool
    call; the React shell listens and re-runs listUseCases(), so a
    freshly authored / refined private template appears in the Ask-tab
    picker + Templates tab within ~1 second, no page reload required.
    The Attachments cache for user_template is invalidated by the
    same event so the Attach picker stays in sync.
  • user_template Attachment type. End users can now attach one
    of their own private templates as a reference in the Ask
    conversation — the picker is server-side restricted to
    sharing=private AND owner_user=<caller> rows, so admins do not
    see other users' private templates through this surface. The LLM
    gets a per-type hint inside the attachment line telling it which
    tool to call (splunk_get_use_case_template_prompt(name=…)) to load
    the attached template's prompt body for discussion / refinement.
  • Per-attachment-type tool hints for the LLM in
    services/claude.ts. Existing types (saved_search, dashboard,
    lookup) gain explicit "resolve via splunk_get_<thing>" hints
    alongside the new user_template line. Reduces guesswork on the
    LLM side when the user attaches an object.

Fixed (verification pass before ship)

A self-review of the authoring path caught five real bugs in the
initial cut. All resolved before 0.9.7 left dev:

  1. REST handler routing — path_info was being equality-matched
    against the stripped sub-segment; on this Splunk version the
    sub-path arrives with the match-prefix included, so every call
    was 404'ing. Switched to substring matching
    ("user_create" in path) to mirror the proven
    bin/itmip_llm_mcp.py pattern.
  2. KVStore POST _key extraction — _post() to KVStore omitted
    ?output_mode=json, so the response came back as XML and the
    _key from json.loads(content) was always empty in the
    dispatcher envelope. Added ?output_mode=json +
    getargs={"output_mode": "json"} + rawResult=True matching
    the MCP handler.
  3. Forbidden-content regex false positives — the role-elevation
    pattern \bset\s+(my|your|the)\s+role\s+to\b matched legitimate
    English ("Set my role to investigate this further"). Tightened
    to require an admin-equivalent target role
    (admin|sc_admin|power|splunk_admin).
  4. Forbidden-content scan was soft. The scan only logged
    matches to attempted_override_fields[] and persisted the
    template anyway. Per spec §4.2 step 6 (body MUST NOT contain ...)
    the scan now adds to errors[] and hard-rejects, so the
    workflow retry loop self-corrects.
  5. Error envelope shape — err(status, {...}) wrapped the body
    under {"error": ...} but the dispatcher reads top-level
    {ok, errors[]}. Worse, the TS splunkFetch throws on non-2xx
    before the dispatcher can read the body, so the LLM saw
    "Splunk REST POST failed: 400" with no detail. Introduced an
    envelope() helper that returns 200 + {ok: false, errors: [...]}
    for validation / quota / ownership failures (the LLM can read
    and self-correct); real 4xx/5xx is reserved for "dispatcher is
    broken" cases (missing auth, KVStore down).

Backup robustness

  • itmip_authoring_changes 404 on fresh installs. Splunk's KVStore
    materialises a collection lazily on first write; on installs where
    no end user has authored a template yet, the new audit collection
    doesn't exist physically and splunk.rest.simpleRequest() raises
    splunk.RESTException with [HTTP 404] <url>. The backup script
    now catches the exception, parses the embedded status code, and
    treats 404 as an empty collection — same semantics as the original
    non-raising branch. Same defence applied to
    bin/itmip_llm_skills.py so a fresh install where itmip_ai_skills
    hasn't been seeded yet falls back to the in-bundle seed catalogue
    cleanly.
  • 503 retry on KVStore startup. _list_collection_rows() in
    bin/itmip_llm_kvstore_backup.py now retries up to 3 times with
    2 / 4 second backoff on 503, which handles the
    ~10-second window after every splunk restart when Mongo is
    warming up. Previously a single transient 503 would fail all 13
    collections in one backup run.
  • Better backup error messages. Non-2xx responses now include
    the first 500 chars of splunkd's response body in the error
    string, so the operator can see exactly why a request was
    refused. Common 503 causes (KVStore disabled, Mongo migration in
    progress, SHC captain re-election) are named in the docstring so
    the troubleshooting path is documented.

Security model

Six-layer defense-in-depth (spec §9): General guardrail → authoring
skill → workflow refusals in Create/Update templates → server-side
forced fields → server-side validation chain → audit trail. The
server is authoritative: any value the LLM emits for
sharing / owner_user / creator / required_roles /
dependent_apps / is_default / is_general / status is silently
overridden and logged.

Deferred to follow-up sessions (documented in

tasks/AUTHORING_HANDOFF.md)

  • Admin promote / demote / delete / direct-edit endpoints (spec §4.3)
  • itmip_authoring_policies KVStore + UI (defaults hard-coded in
    this release; "end users may author" knob is always true per the
    spec default)
  • UI changes: scope filter (Mine / My BU / My Org / Global / All),
    scope pill on tiles, "+ Create template" / "Refine this template"
    buttons, Authoring policies settings page (spec §7)
  • splunk_list_tools_for_authoring REST endpoint — the new
    templates use existing splunk_route_tools for tool discovery
    instead
  • Playwright test suite for the 12 validation scenarios (spec §11)
  • Migration step to physically write sharing / owner_user /
    owner_org_short / owner_bu_short onto pre-0.9.7 rows on disk
    (today the values are derived at read time only — adequate for
    back-compat but a future seed-refresh pass should physicalize them
    so admin queries by sharing field work directly)

0.9.6 — 2026-05-26

Skills layer. Factor reusable "do-it-correctly" prose blocks
(no emojis, dashboard token discipline, MLTK aiasst naming, TrackMe
feed-health verdict, ...) out of individual templates into a new
KVStore-backed itmip_ai_skills collection. Templates reference skills
by name via a new includes_skills field; the runtime concatenates
skill bodies into prompt_text at fetch time inside
splunk_get_use_case_template_prompt. This drops the engineering cost
of "find every template that mentions dashboards and update it to also
say X" from "edit 12+ templates" to "edit one skill". See
instructions/SKILLS_REFACTOR_SPEC.md
and docs/OVERVIEW_TOOLS_AND_TEMPLATES.md §3.5
for the full design + skill catalogue.

Added

  • 18 default skills seeded into itmip_ai_skills on first load:
    general-output-style, spl-perf-priorities, spl-validation-loop,
    dashboard-xml-discipline, dashboard-xml-validation-loop,
    dashboard-studio-versioning, dashboard-proof-required,
    viz-best-fit, alert-companion-dashboard,
    ml-aiasst-naming-and-share, ml-data-readiness-precheck,
    ml-self-correct-budget, feed-health-verdict,
    metric-vs-event-index-aware, read-only-by-default-soc,
    read-only-by-default-itops, data-vs-service-distinction,
    naming-collision-handling.
  • includes_skills field on every default template. 47 of the
    50 default templates declare an ordered list of skills they include
    (the three not declaring any are General, Default, and the
    recommend-only Build / improve a lookup).
  • Skills admin tab (admin-only) between Templates and Tools.
    Lists every skill with title, tags, dependent_apps, status, and
    "used by N templates" column. Admins can view / edit / create /
    soft-delete / hard-delete; non-admins never reach the tab.
  • Auto-include of general-output-style by the runtime
    (Option B in the spec) — every operational template that is not
    General / Default automatically gets this skill prepended without
    needing to list it explicitly.
  • REST handler services/itmip_llm/skills (read-only GET, system
    token) so the dispatcher can resolve includes_skills for any
    authenticated user without requiring the
    list_storage_collections capability. Writes still flow through
    the standard KVStore endpoint with admin-only ACL.
  • KVStore backup + change-log integration for the new
    itmip_ai_skills collection — same daily snapshot + restore +
    change-log treatment that templates already get.

Runtime

  • splunk_get_use_case_template_prompt now returns the assembled
    prompt (skills + template body) rather than the raw prompt_text.
    Dropped skills (missing dep_apps, narrower tenant scope, etc.)
    emit a one-line > Skill X dropped: <reason> note so the LLM can
    adjust narrative without inventing the dropped rule. The tool
    response gains two audit fields: skills_used (ordered list of
    injected skill names) and skills_dropped (per-skill drop reasons).
  • Skill body soft-cap 4000 chars — enforced at create / update
    time in src/services/skills.ts.

Migration notes

  • 0.9.6 ships the infrastructure but does NOT delete the
    duplicated prose     from individual templates' prompt_text. Some
    rules will appear twice in the assembled prompt (once in the
    injected skill, once still in the template body). This is
    functionally safe — the LLM sees the rule twice rather than
    missing it — but prompts will be longer than they need to be until
    the prose-deletion pass lands.
  • The prose deletion (spec Phase 5) is the gating dependency
    for 0.9.7 and requires a snapshot-diff test harness so individual
    template bodies can be trimmed with confidence.
  • Admin-edited templates and skills are immune to seed-refresh.
    Once version > 1 on a row, the auto-refresher leaves it alone.

Cross-references

  • docs/OVERVIEW_TOOLS_AND_TEMPLATES.md rev 3 — new §3.5 with
    architecture diagram + 18-row skill catalogue, new §5.3 / §5.4
    template↔skill indices.
  • docs/RIGHTS_AND_ROLES.md — updated to cover the Skills tab
    admin gate.

0.9.5 — 2026-05-23

Dev-mode TLS-skip toggle for MCP servers, custom HTTP tools, AND
LLM configurations — gated to Splunk Enterprise only (hidden +
refused on Splunk Cloud). Plus a PEM how-to walkthrough in TOOLS.md.
Unblocks local-development testing against splunkd self-signed certs
(the default-config case for the bundled Splunk MCP Server app
and for local Ollama / on-prem LLM endpoints behind self-signed
gateways) without forcing admins to extract and store PEMs that
OpenSSL won't accept as trust anchors anyway.

Added

  • tls_skip_verify boolean on the Edit MCP server, Edit
    custom HTTP tool    , and Edit LLM configuration forms. Disables
    hostname check + cert verification for outbound calls from the
    affected row. Equivalent to NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 in
    Node-land. Gated behind a red warning checkbox + a red banner that
    appears whenever the flag is active. On the LLM editor the checkbox
    only enables in splunk_proxy call mode (browser_direct uses the
    OS trust store). Dev only — never use in production.
  • Splunk Cloud gate (all three surfaces). The checkbox is hidden
    entirely in all three editors on Splunk Cloud, and the dispatcher
    refuses the flag at call time regardless of what's stored in
    KVStore — Cloud admins have no business disabling TLS verification
    on outbound calls; the platform's compliance posture forbids it.
    Detection lives in bin/itmip_llm_guid.is_splunk_cloud(sys_token)
    (cached for the splunkd process lifetime via the same cache the
    License tab uses).
  • tls_verify_skipped audit field in itmip_llm_custom_tool_calls.
    Every MCP + custom-HTTP dispatcher invocation that ran with TLS
    verification disabled is recorded so ops can sweep with
    | inputlookup itmip_llm_custom_tool_calls | where tls_verify_skipped=true.
    LLM-proxy calls log one splunkd.log line per affected call
    (itmip_llm_proxy: tls_verify_skipped=true endpoint=... config=... user=...)
    since the LLM proxy doesn't have its own KVStore audit table.
  • "Working with PEM files" section in docs/TOOLS.md — a
    recipe-driven walkthrough covering: getting the upstream cert with
    openssl s_client, generating a self-signed cert from scratch,
    storing in storage/passwords with --data-urlencode @file so
    newlines survive, verifying the upload via clear_password length,
    proving the PEM with curl --cacert before blaming the dispatcher,
    updating an existing entry, and a complete worked example for the
    Splunk MCP Server on localhost. Now also references the LLM
    surface and calls out the Cloud-gate up front.

Changed

  • Shared HTTP client bin/itmip_llm_http_client.py::build_ssl_context
    takes an optional skip_verify flag. When true, returns an SSL
    context with check_hostname=False and verify_mode=CERT_NONE.
    The PEM, if also supplied, is still loaded (but ignored for
    verification when skip is on). build_request plumbs the flag
    through to the new signature.
  • bin/itmip_llm_mcp.py:
    _decode_server / _encode_server now persist tls_skip_verify,
    McpClient.__init__ takes skip_verify, _build_mcp_client_for_server
    forwards it, and every audit row from the dispatcher records the
    effective value as tls_verify_skipped. Cloud-gate at the same
    spot rejects the flag (and emits a splunkd.log warning) on Cloud.
  • bin/itmip_llm_custom_tools.py: the HTTP dispatcher reads
    impl.tls_skip_verify, applies the same Cloud-gate, forwards to
    build_request, and propagates through _http_invoke's internal
    outcome into the audit row.
  • bin/itmip_llm_proxy.py: parallel-ported _build_ssl_context /
    _build_request got the same skip_verify flag (the LLM proxy
    predates the shared client and keeps its own urllib path).
    Cloud-gate at the call site rejects the flag and falls back to
    full verification, emitting a splunkd.log warning per refused call.
  • bin/itmip_llm_guid.py: new is_splunk_cloud(sys_token) helper
    exported and used by all three dispatchers. Cached via the same
    get_environment_guid cache (TTL = 24h).
  • default/collections.conf: [itmip_mcp_servers] declares
    field.tls_skip_verify = bool, [itmip_llm_configs] declares
    the same field for LLM configs, and [itmip_llm_custom_tool_calls]
    declares field.tls_verify_skipped = bool. Custom tools store
    the flag inside implementation_json, so no new field on
    [itmip_llm_custom_tools].

Demoted

  • "Build a Dashboard Studio JSON dashboard" template demoted from
    operational → draft. Studio JSON output isn't reliable enough
    to ship as the default path — render-validation false positives
    and edge-case Studio shapes still bite. The short_description
    now opens with a [DRAFT — ...] marker so the LLM router and
    the Ask tab tile both make the status visible. Use the Simple
    XML dashboard template for production work until this is
    promoted back. Edit applied to both seed sources — the JSON
    seed (default/data/seeds/itmip_ai_use_cases.json) for fresh
    installs and the TS SEED_TEMPLATES array
    (src/services/useCases.ts) for the auto-reseed-on-page-load
    loop that revives system-unedited templates.
  • New doc: docs/DASHBOARD_STUDIO_JSON.md — full pipeline map
    (template → builder tools → persistence → validation chain →
    on-disk artifact), the version cheat-sheet, every known failure
    mode we've hit with root cause + fix location, the canonical
    edit order when changing the pipeline, and the explicit
    promotion criteria for moving the template back to operational.
    Cross-linked from docs/TOOLS.md (dashboard category row),
    docs/ADMIN_MANUAL.md (Where to go next), and the template's
    own short_description.

Runtime quality engine — Week 1 foundation (Studio JSON)

The first slice of the runtime quality engine described in
instructions/RUNTIME_QUALITY_BRIEF.md. Per the brief, the Studio
template stays in draft until the full 5-stage pipeline lands and
the §15 acceptance metrics are met. This release ships Stage 2
(deterministic auto-fixes) in isolation — the foundation that every
later stage depends on.

  • New module: src/services/studioAutoFixes.ts —
    the AUTO_FIXES array with AF-STUDIO-001 through AF-STUDIO-005,
    one entry per mechanically-fixable §6 failure mode in
    docs/DASHBOARD_STUDIO_JSON.md. Each entry has a detector
    (returns JSONPath strings naming offences) and a fixer (returns the
    corrected JSON plus a change log). The applyAutoFixes() driver
    loops until a full pass produces no changes, capped at 5 iterations.
  • assembleDefinition() in src/services/studioBuilder.ts
    now applies the auto-fixes before returning. Belt-and-braces: the
    builder already enforces these shapes by construction, so the report
    is normally clean: true. The auto-fix layer catches future builder
    regressions, hand-crafted JSON paths that bypass the builder, and
    JSON loaded from external sources (import / clone).
  • New sibling export assembleDefinitionWithReport() + matching
    builderPreviewWithReport() — same as the plain versions but also
    returns the AutoFixReport so callers (publish, future bootstrap,
    debug surfaces) can see which AF-STUDIO-NNN entries fired.
  • splunk_builder_publish and splunk_builder_preview tool
    results     now include an auto_fix_report field
    ({ clean, total_fixes_applied, changes[] }) so the LLM and the
    reviewing human see what was silently corrected.
  • docs/DASHBOARD_STUDIO_JSON.md updates:
  • §6.1 through §6.5 now carry auto-fix AF-STUDIO-NNN cross-link
    suffixes next to the section headers. §6.6 / §6.7 carry "no
    auto-fix" notes with their reason.
  • New §12 "Runtime quality engine" — short intro to the 5-stage
    plan, the per-stage current status table, and the §6 ↔
    AF-STUDIO-NNN correspondence rule.
  • New plan doc: tasks/RUNTIME_QUALITY_ROLLOUT.md —
    the week-by-week plan for Weeks 2-8 with checkboxes per
    deliverable, the cross-cutting decisions locked at v0.9.5 (notably:
    Signal B JSON Schema will be pulled from the running splunkd at
    bootstrap rather than vendored), and the file-by-file inventory
    matching brief §13.3.

This is a silent improvement — no UX change, no template promotion
yet. The template short_description continues to carry the
[DRAFT — ...] marker. Auto-fixes apply uniformly to all Studio JSON
flowing through the builder, including imports and the existing
operational Simple XML path (which doesn't touch Studio JSON).

Out of scope (deferred)

  • Silent except Exception: pass in build_ssl_context for malformed
    PEMs — should at minimum log to splunkd.log so a bad PEM doesn't
    masquerade as a generic CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED. Tracked in
    tasks/todo.md v0.9.5 follow-ups.
  • Pattern-match TLS errors in the dispatcher and rewrite to "TLS
    verification failed — set TLS CA ref or enable dev-mode skip
    (Outbound network section)" so admins get a pointer to the fix
    without grepping splunkd.log. Tracked alongside the above.
  • Dedicated audit-log collection for LLM proxy calls (parallel to
    itmip_llm_custom_tool_calls). Currently LLM calls only land in
    the token-cost telemetry index via itmip_llm_usage_log.py. For
    now the dev-mode skip emits structured splunkd.log lines which
    cover the "did anyone use this in prod?" audit use case.

0.9.4 — 2026-05-22

Multi-tenant clarity + Orgs/BUs polish. No schema changes — the
existing AND semantics between Org app_patterns and role_patterns,
and between a template's Org and BU, are unchanged; this release makes
them visible in the UI and shores up the edge cases.

Added

  • Unassigned-user overlay. A non-admin user who lands in the
    Workbench but does NOT resolve into any configured Organisation now
    sees a greyed-out app with an admin-configurable message ("contact
    your Splunk team to request access"). The text is read from
    [ui] unassigned_message in local/itmip_ai_workbench.conf — a
    generic default ships pre-populated. Admins are never marked
    unassigned (they fall through to DFLT/DFLT so they can recover).
  • "Multi-tenant namespace model" section added to
    docs/USER_MANUAL.md, docs/ADMIN_MANUAL.md,
    docs/FUNCTIONALITY.md, and docs/installation_instructions.md,
    documenting that AiWorkbench is designed to be embedded in every
    Splunk app's nav menu, runs in the calling app's namespace, and
    auto-resolves Org/BU from (callingApp, userRoles).
  • New troubleshooting entry: "User sees a greyed-out AiWorkbench
    with a 'contact your Splunk team' message" with the admin fix.

Fixed

  • + BU button in Orgs & BUs did nothing on Orgs with an empty
    SHORT.     The conditional (creatingBuOrg || editingBu) evaluated
    empty string as falsy and skipped the modal. Now uses !== null
    and explicitly errors if the Org has no SHORT before opening the
    modal. License-cap blocking the button is now also surfaced inline
    ("+ BU (license cap)" + tooltip + visible disabled styling).
  • Removing * (or any chip) from a PatternMultiSelect was
    unreliable.     The chip's × was a text node inside the same span
    that handled click — overlapping text-selection / hover behaviour
    intercepted the click in some browsers. The × is now a real
    <button> with hover affordance, explicit stopPropagation, and
    an aria-label.
  • "nothing selected yet" placeholder in PatternMultiSelect was
    misleading for fields where empty = "no constraint applied".     The
    component now accepts an emptyHint prop; each call site supplies
    field-specific copy:
  • Template editor → "Required Splunk apps" empty: "No app
    prerequisites — template visible regardless of installed apps."
  • Template editor → "Required Splunk roles" empty: "No role
    requirement — template visible to every role (within the Org +
    BU scope above)."
  • Org editor → "App patterns" empty: "⚠ empty — this Org never
    matches any app. Add at least one pattern (or * for all)."
  • Org editor → "Role patterns" empty: same warning shape.

Changed (UI clarity)

  • Orgs & BUs page banner now explicitly states the AND semantics:
    "A user resolves into this Org only if the calling Splunk app
    matches at least one App pattern AND the user has at least one role
    matching the Role patterns. The built-in DFLT Org catches all apps
    for admins; users who don't resolve into any Org see a greyed-out
    app with an admin-configurable message."
  • Org editor inline AND-semantics callout above the App patterns
    / Role patterns fields.
  • Template editor → Visibility fieldset now shows a callout
    explaining single-select Org + single-select BU semantics with the
    DFLT wildcard table (DFLT/DFLT = everyone, OrgX/DFLT = anyone in
    OrgX, OrgX/SOC = only OrgX/SOC) and the "clone the template" hint
    for multi-Org coverage.
  • "Required Splunk apps" label expanded to make explicit that the
    check honours the user's per-app ACL — an app installed system-wide
    but invisible to the user (no read permission) still hides the
    template.

Configuration

  • New [ui] stanza in default/itmip_ai_workbench.conf:
  • unassigned_message — message shown to non-admin users with no
    matching Org. Default text references "your Splunk administration
    team"; customers SHOULD override this in local/ with their real

Security model (recap)

Custom tools are a powerful primitive — admins can wire the LLM up
to any HTTP API in the organisation. The release is designed so the
blast radius of a mistake or a compromised admin account is bounded:

  • Tool definitions can only be written by admins. End users see them
    in the LLM's tool list but cannot edit.
  • Secrets live in storage/passwords and are resolved server-side
    on every call. The definition can be exported and shared safely —
    the secret stays per-environment.
  • allowed_hosts is a per-tool allowlist enforced after template
    substitution so a parameter-driven URL can't reach an unintended
    host (SSRF defence).
  • RFC1918 and loopback hosts are refused by default — admins must
    set allow_internal: true to wire up internal-network tools.
  • Every invocation is audited with the calling user, the tool, a
    hash of the arguments, the outcome, and the duration.

    allow-list, rate limit, audit trail), and the accepted residual
    risk (users can globally share their own AI-Assistent-trained
    models; not the model's source data).

0.3.0 — 2026-05-14

The "make it commercial" release. Adds licensing, multi-tenancy
enforcement, corporate-IAM integration, role-specific user guides, and
a re-audited security baseline. Builds cleanly through Splunk
AppInspect.

Added

  • Cryptolens licensing end-to-end. Admin-only License tab in
    the Web UI activates a 25-character key, validates against
    Cryptolens, removes a stored licence, and manages expiry-warning
    email recipients. Browser-direct activation flow works on air-gapped
    Search Heads — the SH never has to reach the licensing vendor.
  • Five licence tiers:
  • Personal (free, no key required): 1 Org, 1 BU, 1 concurrent ask
    session, no History, no Tokens & Costs.
  • Professional: 1 Org, 3 BUs, full features. Node-locked.
  • Enterprise: 1 Org, unlimited BUs. Node-locked.
  • MSP: unlimited Orgs + BUs. One key activates against multiple
    Splunk environments     up to the vendor-set machine cap.
  • PoV (time-limited) and NFR (Not-for-Resale, MSP features, 1
    year, no node lock) variants supported. Both render a badge next
    to the app title.
  • Tier-aware caps on Orgs & BUs. UI disables + Add Org and
    + BU at cap; server-side enforcement at
    /services/itmip_llm/tenancy (new persistent REST handler) is the
    authoritative boundary. Admins who bypass via raw KVStore still hit
    no soft error today, but the UI / API surface is consistent.
  • Customer authorisation hook. Drop a Python file at
    local/bin/customer_authorisation.py and the Splunk-side proxy
    invokes it before every outbound LLM request to mint fresh headers
    from a corporate IAM gateway (WebEAM.Next, Ping, Okta, AzureAD,
    internal SAML…). Documented per-LLM toggle in the Settings UI.
  • License-expiry alert auto-creation. Saving recipient emails on
    the License tab creates a Splunk Enterprise saved alert
    (itmip_llm_license_expiry_warning) that fires when the licence is
    within 30 days of expiring. Scripted input
    bin/itmip_llm_license_monitor.py runs every 6 h and is silent
    until the threshold is crossed.
  • AI Toolkit model-namespace handling. The 5 MLTK templates
    (outlier, multi-field anomaly, forecasting, clustering, prediction)
    now write their training and scoring saved searches into
    Splunk_ML_Toolkit with global sharing, then call the new
    splunk_share_mltk_model_globally tool so dashboards / alerts in any
    app can apply <model> cleanly. Companion dashboards still live in
    the user's current app.
  • New LLM tools:
  • splunk_create_saved_search / splunk_update_saved_search gained
    target_app and target_sharing parameters.
  • splunk_share_mltk_model_globally — promotes a
    __mlspl_<name>.{csv,mlmodel,onnx} lookup-table-file to
    owner=nobody, sharing=global, app=Splunk_ML_Toolkit.
  • Role-specific manuals version-stamped 0.3.0:
  • docs/installation_instructions.md — fresh-install walkthrough.
  • docs/USER_MANUAL.md — for end users.
  • docs/ADMIN_MANUAL.md — for admin / sc_admin.
  • Playwright web-UI test suite (tests/playwright/): 23 specs
    covering app boot, role-gating, template editor, LLM config modal,
    License tab visibility + content, customer auth hook checkbox. CI
    friendly; runnable locally with npx playwright test.
  • Python unit tests for the customer-auth invoker, licence tier
    resolver, GUID resolver, and tenancy cap enforcer (33 tests total).

Changed

  • App label renamed in default/app.conf to "AI Assistent for
    Splunk".
  • All 27 use-case templates now ship as status = operational
    (previously 21 were draft and admin-only on the Ask tab). Existing
    installs auto-promote on first page-load after upgrade via the
    refreshSystemEntry loop.
  • Bootstrap Anthropic LLM (DFLT_DFLT_anthropic_central)
    defaults to call_mode = splunk_proxy so the central key never
    reaches the browser. Users with the bootstrap config don't need
    their own key once an admin stores the central one.
  • Tokens & Costs event sourcetype + cost-estimator pull per-model
    pricing from src/services/llm/providers.ts. Cost numbers now
    reflect the actual model the user picked, not a fixed Sonnet rate.
  • SplunkApiError.message now surfaces the server-side error
    body verbatim (e.g. "License 'professional' allows up to 3 BU(s)
    per Org; 'ACME' already has 3."    ) so the UI shows actionable copy
    instead of generic 4xx text.
  • Security audit doc (docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md)
    rewritten as a status board: every prior BLOCKER / HIGH is marked
    RESOLVED with the iteration that fixed it; new findings from
    customer-auth hook / licensing / tenancy wrapper added.
  • docs/FUNCTIONALITY.md updated with a "What's new in 0.3.0"
    section and cross-links to the new manuals.

Fixed

  • License-expiry saved alert was created but never sent email.
    Splunk Enterprise 9.x needs both actions = email (to enable the
    action) and action.email.* parameters (to configure it); only the
    latter was being written. The alert now lights up the "Send email"
    trigger action in the UI.
  • License-expiry alert SPL had no index=. Switched to a new
    ai_assistant_license_index macro that resolves to
    index=main sourcetype=itmip_llm_license by default and can be
    overridden in local/macros.conf to route into a dedicated index.
  • Removing every recipient email left a dead alert behind. Now
    saving an empty recipient list deletes the saved alert outright
    instead of leaving one that fires and emails no one.
  • make spl packaging deleted the React bundle after it finished
    archiving (a side effect of force-adding appserver/static/build/
    on a temp branch + git checkout - to the original branch). The
    Makefile now re-runs npm run build at the very end so the local
    Splunk install stays in a runnable state after every packaging run.
  • Makefile was being shipped in the .spl, tripping AppInspect's
    check_destructive_commands on its dev-cleanup rm -rf
    instructions. Added Makefile export-ignore to .gitattributes
    and switched git archive to --worktree-attributes so the
    exclusion takes effect without needing a commit first.
  • AI Toolkit dashboards generated from outside the Splunk_ML_Toolkit
    app threw "Failed to load model — Model does not exist".     The
    template flow now pins the training + scoring saved searches to
    Splunk_ML_Toolkit + global sharing, then explicitly promotes the
    model file so apply resolves from any calling app.
  • MIME-type / 404 errors at the React shell when
    appserver/static/build/main.js was missing post-rename or
    post-make spl. Documented in
    tasks/lessons.md and now self-healing via the
    Makefile fix above.
  • CSRF silent fallback in splunkFetch removed — state-changing
    requests now throw a clear SplunkApiError(status=0) when the
    token cookie is missing, instead of degrading to an unauthenticated
    request that splunkd will reject far downstream.

Security

  • All 5 BLOCKER + 9 HIGH findings from the v0.2.x audit are
    resolved.     Highlights:
  • /services/itmip_llm/secret POST/DELETE now requires admin
    server-side; GET is rate-limited and gated on per-LLM allow-list.
  • /services/itmip_llm/proxy no longer accepts caller-supplied
    endpoint; uses the stored LlmConfig.endpoint. Caller-supplied
    extra_headers filtered against a 3-entry allow-list.
  • /services/itmip_llm/api_key admin-only; bootstrap LLM defaults
    to splunk_proxy so the key stays on the SH.
  • KVStore collection ACLs for itmip_llm_configs,
    itmip_organisations, itmip_business_units,
    itmip_tool_assignments, itmip_llm_license tightened to
    read/write: [admin, power / sc_admin].
  • SPL injection guard: rejectSideEffectSpl() runs inside every
    LLM-dispatched search and refuses outputlookup, outputcsv,
    sendemail, sendalert, collect, summaryindex, tscollect,
    metasearch, script, runshellscript, delete.
  • Dashboard XML lint refuses <script>, <iframe>, <object>,
    <embed>, javascript: URLs, inline event handlers.
  • Per-user rate limits added to the most-spammable endpoints (30/min
    on secret GET + proxy, 120/min on usage_log).
  • The full status board is in docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md.

Removed

  • Legacy v0.1 "Anthropic API key" card under Settings. The
    storage path (storage/passwords realm = itmip_ai_splunk_assistent_app,
    name = anthropic_api_key) is still read transparently by
    loadSecretForConfig() as a fallback for the bootstrap LLM, so
    existing installs that pre-date the rename keep working.

Known limitations

  • Concurrent-session enforcement on the Personal tier is UI-only —
    cross-browser hard enforcement needs a heartbeat protocol.
  • The Cryptolens product access token is embedded in code (this is
    the vendor-recommended pattern — it is the product's read-only
    API key, not a customer secret). A scanner may flag it; document
    the rationale on Splunkbase submission if asked.

0.2.x — internal release stream

A series of internal iterations between 2026-03 and 2026-05-12 leading
up to 0.3.0. Highlights worth knowing if you're upgrading from a
pre-0.3.0 build:

Added (during 0.2.x)

  • Multi-LLM support: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Groq, Gemini,
    Bedrock, Ollama, OpenRouter. Pick provider + model per LLM
    configuration.
  • Two call modes per LLM: browser_direct (lowest latency,
    CORS-limited) and splunk_proxy (works everywhere, keys
    server-side).
  • Streaming responses for Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible providers.
  • Multi-tenant Organisations + Business Units. Templates and LLM
    configs scope per Org/BU. Resolved per page load from the user's
    Splunk app + role.
  • Use-case templates for SPL searches, Simple XML dashboards,
    Dashboard Studio JSON, alerts (with companion dashboards), saved
    searches, reports, lookups, field extractions, plus 10 Splunk AI
    Toolkit pipelines.
  • Tokens & Costs tab — multi-axis side-by-side cost analytics
    (App / User / Model / Provider / Org / BU / LLM config) over time.
  • Tools tab — per-Org/BU enable/disable of every LLM tool.
  • TLS CA certificate (PEM) upload per LLM (server-side proxy
    honours customer-internal CAs).
  • Extra HTTP headers per LLM (static tokens, customer-internal
    gateway headers).
  • KVStore-backed user history with per-question template / LLM /
    provider / model / token / cost attribution and clickable links to
    every created knowledge object.

Renamed (during 0.2.x)

  • App id stayed itmip_ai_splunk_assistent_app; label evolved from
    "Claude Assistant for Splunk" → "AI User Assistent for Splunk" →
    (in 0.3.0) "AI Assistent for Splunk".
  • All bin/itmip_claude_*.py Python handlers renamed to
    bin/itmip_llm_*.py. Legacy URLs (/services/itmip_claude/*)
    retired; new ones live under /services/itmip_llm/*.

0.1.x — pre-history

The original "Claude Assistant for Splunk" with a single Anthropic
provider and a hand-stored API key under storage/passwords realm =
itmip_ai_splunk_assistent_app, name = anthropic_api_key. The
legacy key path is still readable by the bootstrap LLM in 0.3.x for
backward compatibility — no migration step needed.


Short Description:
A workbench for Splunk, not just a chatbot. Analyse, correlate and build across SPL, dashboards, alerts, AI Toolkit / MLTK, ES, ITSI and TrackMe through tools that understand each one — plus any MCP server you add. Pick your LLM: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Groq, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama, OpenRouter. Multi-tenant, multi-tier (Free, Pro, Enterprise, MSP).


Description:
AI Workbench is a generative workspace for Splunk. Not a chatbot bolted onto search but a real workbench, where you investigate, analyse and build using tools that understand Splunk natively. The Workbench is built as a host shell. It has no use-cases of its own — it derives everything from the Splunk app a user opens it from and the Splunk roles they hold. Install it once on the Search Head, then embed it into the apps your users already live in: Search, ITSI, Enterprise Security, your SOC apps, your MSP customer apps. The same engine renders a different experience per calling app, with different templates, different LLMs, different tools, and writes its outputs into that calling app's namespace. End users never leave the app they came from. Ask in plain English. Get back validated SPL searches, Simple XML dashboards, alerts, lookups, reports and Splunk AI Toolkit (MLTK) pipelines. Every artefact is run for real before it is saved, and every artefact is a normal Splunk knowledge object — owned by the calling user, in the calling app, findable in Splunk's own UI. The depth is the difference. Where a generic MCP-only assistant talks to Splunk through one broad door, AI Workbench ships with fine-grained, Splunk-aware tools across Core, Enterprise Security, ITSI, TrackMe and the AI Toolkit — roughly fifty of them, each scoped to one job a Splunk admin actually does. The LLM picks the right tool for the question, runs it under your existing Splunk ACLs, and shows its work. Extend it further by adding HTTP tools or registering any MCP server in the Tools tab. Two audiences benefit immediately. Splunk users who know what they want but find SPL foreign get production-quality searches and dashboards generated and validated panel-by-panel. Splunk users who bounce off MLTK get an outlier detector, forecaster, classifier or clusterer built end-to-end, with a companion dashboard that proves the model is doing something sensible. Bring your own LLM: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Groq, Google Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Ollama (local, fully offline) or OpenRouter. Browser-direct for speed, or Splunk-server-side proxy mode so API keys never leave the search head. Bring your own corporate IAM — WebEAM.Next, Ping, Okta, AzureAD, internal SAML — via a customer-supplied Python hook that mints fresh auth headers per request. Multi-tenant by design. Organisations and Business Units are resolved automatically from the calling app and the user's roles — end users don't pick a tenant. Templates, LLM configurations and tool availability all scope per Org or BU. Run one Splunk environment for many teams or many customers without them seeing each other. Tokens and Costs breaks spend down by App, User, Model, Provider, Organisation, BU or LLM configuration — over time, with real per-model pricing. Free, Professional, Enterprise and MSP licence tiers, activated self-serve, air-gap-friendly.

item.title: AI Query Assistant for Splunk - v4.0.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

Release Notes

v4.0.0 — Conversational AI Query Assistant

Ask Splunk questions in plain language. v4 turns the app from a one-shot NL→SPL translator into a real conversational assistant.

WHAT'S NEW

  • Multi-turn conversations — Every query belongs to a thread. Ask a follow-up that omits earlier context, such as “now show me just the top 3 by count”, and the agent remembers the index, time range, and filters from the previous turn. Switch between recent conversations from a dropdown, or start fresh with “+ New”.

  • Clarifying questions — When your question is too vague to answer well, the agent flags it and asks for specifics instead of guessing. Answer inline and refine on the same thread.

  • Result narration (opt-in) — The agent reads the rows returned by your SPL and writes a 2–3 sentence summary, highlights key findings with actual numbers, and suggests follow-up searches.

  • Supervisor pipeline (opt-in) — Turn on a 4-subagent flow: planner → schema_resolver → spl_generator → auditor, for tougher queries. The schema_resolver grounds SPL in your actual indexes, sourcetypes, and fields, helping reduce hallucinated data source or field names. The auditor provides an independent safety review before the SPL runs.

  • Google Gemini provider — First-class support for Gemini 1.5 / 2.0 / 2.5, including both Google AI Studio with an API key and Vertex AI with a project and service account, alongside the existing OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic adapters.

  • Smarter Query Templates — Templates now carry an SPL pattern plus searchable tags. When your question matches a saved template, the agent adapts the template’s SPL to your current intent and tells you which template it used.

SAFETY

  • Pre-flight checks: Dangerous keywords such as delete, drop, purge, truncate, wipe, and shutdown are blocked before any LLM call, avoiding API spend on requests that would not be allowed to run.

  • Post-flight checks: Generated SPL is scanned for write operations such as | outputlookup, | delete, | script, | collect, and | sendalert, as well as unbounded time ranges and sensitive-field references. Dangerous SPL is refused; risky-but-readable SPL is downgraded to a yellow caution badge.

  • Independent LLM audit: In supervisor mode, the app performs a second independent safety review before SPL ever reaches the executor.

RELIABILITY

  • Automatic retries on transient LLM errors — Supports automatic retries for Cloudflare 429, brief 5xx errors, and gateway timeouts. A single network blip no longer fails the whole query.

  • Append-only conversation history — Keeps long-lived threads responsive by storing conversation history in an append-only model.

  • Structured logs — Every query records latency, token usage, subagent transitions, and guardrail decisions. These logs can be indexed in _internal as event=agentic.* for Splunk-on-Splunk dashboards.

COMPATIBILITY

  • Dual-path compatibility — Runs on every Splunk 10.x version. Splunk 10.0 / 10.1 keep v3 behavior, so NL→SPL continues to work as before. Splunk 10.2+ on Python 3.13 automatically enables all new features with no additional configuration required.

UPGRADE PROCEDURE

  1. Stop Splunk.

  2. Install the new app:

splunk install app AI_Query_Assistant_for_Splunk_v4.0.0.tar.gz -update 1
  1. On Splunk 10.2+, pull agentic dependencies:
splunk cmd python3.13 $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/AI_Query_Assistant_for_Splunk/bin/install_deps.py
  1. Run the one-time migration:
splunk cmd python3.13 $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/AI_Query_Assistant_for_Splunk/bin/migrate_v3_to_v4.py
  1. Start Splunk.

Existing AI Provider records, query history, and license activation carry forward unchanged.

BUG FIXES vs v3.0.7

  • Risk-level audit verdict is now reliably attached to the response.

  • Anthropic-compatible providers whose base URL omits /v1, such as Volcengine Ark, now authenticate correctly instead of returning 401.

  • Conversation history records are written correctly even when message content contains LLM-specific binary block types.

  • Dangerous-keyword detection now works through the new async pipeline.

  • SSL trust store fallback now works when SSL_CERT_FILE points to a missing path.

LICENSE

Online activation against:

https://license.reallysec.com

Existing v3 license keys remain valid for v4.

Trial license: contact support@reallysec.com with your Server GUID and company email.

Issues / feedback: support@reallysec.com


Short Description:
Use natural language to generate SPL queries in Splunk with support for multiple AI providers, query history, templates, and enterprise security guardrails.


Description:
AI Query Assistant for Splunk is an AI-powered app that enables users to query and analyze Splunk data using natural language. It helps convert plain-language questions into structured SPL searches, reducing the learning curve for SPL and improving analyst efficiency. The app is designed for security operations, IT operations, and data exploration scenarios where users need faster and more intuitive access to Splunk data. It supports multiple AI providers, including OpenAI-compatible APIs and Anthropic Claude, and provides configurable safeguards to help reduce the risk of unsafe or invalid query generation. Key capabilities include natural language to SPL conversion, AI provider management, query history, reusable query templates, and controlled enterprise usage with license-based activation. This app is intended for organizations that want to improve Splunk usability while maintaining operational control and security.

### Fixed: Map panel stuck on infinite loading after rapid filter change

Reported by Ambulance Australia.

When a user changed or cleared a dashboard filter while the map panel was still rendering its previous result set, the panel could stop showing markers and keep its loading spinner visible indefinitely. The map only recovered when the user clicked the panel's Refresh button. Most reliably observed on dashboards with multiple cascading filters where the user can change a second filter while the first one's results are still streaming in.

The Gigamon App for Federated Search S3 is designed for customers who want pre-built dashboards, federated searches, and pipeline templates that provide deep visibility into security, operations, and compliance use cases while controlling Splunk ingest costs. PCI Compliance Use Case This app supports security, operations, and compliance use cases, with PCI compliance as one important example enabled by its tiered data strategy. 1. Send the necessary high-value data to the Splunk hot tier for immediate monitoring, detections, and operational dashboards. 2. Send the full JSON data stream to AWS S3 as the cold tier for lower-cost long-term retention. 3. Use Splunk Federated Search to query the data in S3 whenever audit, investigation, or compliance reporting is required. How it helps 1. Hot tier for immediate visibility The app keeps the most relevant PCI and security data in Splunk so teams can monitor in-scope environments, investigate active issues, and use pre-built dashboards without waiting on rehydration. 2. Cold tier for full-fidelity retention The complete JSON data set is stored in AWS S3, allowing organizations to retain broader telemetry and historical evidence without sending everything into Splunk hot storage. 3. Reduced ingestion cost By sending only the required data to Splunk and landing the full JSON feed in S3, the app helps reduce unnecessary ingest and supports a more cost-efficient retention model. 4. Federated access for compliance audits When PCI audits, quarterly reviews, or historical investigations are required, teams can use Splunk Federated Search to access the retained JSON data in S3 directly from the Splunk. Example For a PCI compliance deployment, an organization can send the most critical monitoring data to Splunk for day-to-day visibility while storing all JSON in AWS S3. When an audit or compliance review happens, the retained data in S3 can be queried through Federated Search to support PCI reporting and investigation.

item.title: InSitzes App for Splunk Enterprise Monitoring - v3.0.16 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Short Description:
Unified Splunk Enterprise monitoring in one React dashboard: 31 automated health checks, hourly SVC estimation for Splunk Cloud cost modeling, license tracking, ingestion anomaly detection, full-stack CPU/memory/disk visibility, and scheduled-search and workload analysis.


Description:
The InSitzes App for Splunk Enterprise is a unified monitoring suite that gives administrators actionable insight into ingestion, system performance, workload management, search efficiency, and compute consumption across their Splunk Enterprise deployment. Rather than stitching together the Monitoring Console, license pages, introspection data, and ad-hoc searches, admins get one React-powered dashboard with purpose-built tabs to answer the questions that matter most: Is my environment healthy? Is data flowing reliably? Are searches running efficiently? Am I approaching my license quota? And what would my workload cost under Splunk Cloud compute-based licensing? The Health tab runs 31 automated checks across 8 categories — System, Ingestion, Data Quality, Search, Compute, Workload, Forwarding, and Capacity — with weighted severity scoring and a rolled-up environment health score so you know immediately where to focus. Individual tabs drill into CPU, memory, and disk utilization across every server role (search heads, indexers, cluster manager, deployment server, SHC deployer); live license usage with 7-day trend against daily quota; forwarder throughput, HEC health, SSL and deployment-client issues; sourcetype parsing, timestamp, and debug-event quality; scheduled search execution, skip reasons, and wasteful-search detection; WLM filtered, reclassified, and aborted search rates; and dashboard refresh frequency with base vs. chained search analysis. The Compute tab delivers an hourly-computed SVC estimate — via the bundled insitzes_svc_estimation saved search and dynamic role discovery on _introspection data — so Enterprise admins can see exactly what their workload would cost under Splunk Cloud compute-based licensing, broken down by search head, app, search type, user, and provenance, with an optional Cost Mode. Install on your Monitoring Console search head; ingestion data is read live from _internal license_usage events, eliminating scheduled-lookup maintenance. Pre-built alert saved searches (disabled by default) cover ingestion anomalies, app updates, large lookup files, and redundant scheduled searches.

The InSitzes App for Splunk Cloud is a unified monitoring suite that gives administrators actionable insight into ingestion, system performance, workload management, search efficiency, storage, and compute consumption across their Splunk Cloud environment.
